In daily analysis, do you often encounter the following problems?


* What is the maximum number of concurrent apps?

* What is the maximum number of viewers during the live broadcast?

* How long do users spend browsing different pages?

* How many pages do users visit each time they visit? How long is the visit?

* Different activity pages, which page effect is better, bounce rate is lower?

* Which page did the user leave last?

* How long does a user use a feature module?


……

The above problems can be solved through the session, let's understand the concept of the next session together.

<span id="_1-概述"></span>
# 1. Overview

<span id="_1-1-session是什么"></span>
## 1.1 What is a session?

Session is a conversation, and users will engage in a series of behavioral interactions from the beginning to the end of the visit, such as clicking buttons, browsing pages, etc. This series of behavioral interactions constitutes a conversation. A person can have multiple conversations, and the end of the conversation depends on the cutting time.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

<span id="_1-2-session切割时间"></span>
## 1.2 session cutting time

The session cut time is the longest acceptable time interval between two events when they are triggered. If the time interval between the two actions exceeds the cutting time, the session is cut. It can also be understood that when the user performs an action and does not perform a follow\-up action after the cutting time, the access session is considered to have ended. After that, other behaviors are started, which is regarded as the start of another new session. On the basis of the transaction table, the generated session_id correlates the single point behavior events of the same user, and finally forms a session composed of a sequence of events.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

For example, in the picture, user A starts to open the App at 10:52 am, first searches, 2 minutes later, starts to browse the activity page, 6 minutes later, searches again, it is already 11 am, gets off work time, and colleagues go out for lunch for 1h, go back to the previous search results page, start browsing the product details page, and find that it is not what you want, so change a few keywords, repeat the search, and finally find the product you want, browse the product details page again, and feel very like it, collect the product, the end of the visit.

Suppose we set the cutting time to 30 minutes, user A has two sessions, and user A has no follow\-up behavior for 30 minutes after the second search, so the first session ends at 11:30 am. When the user starts accessing again at 12 o'clock, the second session has already started.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">The session cutting time is not the maximum (long) time range of the session, so be sure to distinguish it.</div>


<span id="_1-3-为什么需要session分析？"></span>
## 1.3 Why is session analysis required?

When users want to understand metrics such as "visits", "average interaction depth", "usage time", "stay time", "bounce rate", "exit rate", etc., they need to introduce sessions to analyze. The custom session analysis in BytePlus Growth Analysis quickly supports session\-related analysis.

<span id="_2-session计算原理"></span>
# 2. Principle of session calculation

As shown in the figure, there are three users: Xiaohuo, Xiaoshan, and Xiaotiao, which correspond to the events that occur in chronological order for each user. A/B/C/D/E can represent different events or different pages. The duration in the middle is the length of the interval between the two events.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

Assume that the session cutting time is 30min, Xiaohuo has 2 sessions, Xiaoshan has 2 sessions, and Xiaojump has 1 session.

Respectively:


|user |session |
|---|---|
|Small fire |session1:[A\-B\-A\-C]session2:[D\-B] |
|hill |session3:[E\-C\-A]session4:[A] |
|Little jump |session5:[C] |


Some examples of computable indicators and principles in the figure are as follows:


|**Calculation index** |**Calculation principle** |**The principle of calculating indicators in the figure** |**The results of the calculated indicators in the figure** |
|---|---|---|---|
|Total number of sessions |The sum of sessions that occurred according to the cutting rule. |Xiaohuo had two conversations, Xiaoshan had two conversations, and Xiaotiao had one conversation. |5 |
|Total number of sessions |The sum of the number of sessions deduplicated according to the cutting rule. |Xiaohuo, Xiaoshan, Xiaojump three users |3 |
|Number of sessions per capita |Total number of sessions divided by total number of people |5/3 |5/3 |
|Concurrent users |In a certain period of time, the number of sessions that occur simultaneously in a session goes to the sum of weights. |Suppose these three sessions occur at the same time period |3 |
|Bounce rate |The total number of sessions in a session is 1 divided by the total number of sessions. Refers to the proportion of users who enter a website or page and leave without any further action. The bounce rate is mainly concerned with whether the user continues to browse other content or perform other actions after entering the page. |A session in which the number of events in the session is 1 has session4 of the hill and session5 of the small jump, so the numerator is 2 and the denominator is 5, 2/5 = 40% |40% |
|A event exit rate |The number of sessions ended by this event divided by the total number of A events refers to the proportion of sessions in a session that users end with an event. A high exit rate for an event may indicate that the user left the website or app after completing a specific event. |There are session3 and session4 sessions that end with the A event; the total number of A events is 4, so the A event exit rate = 2/4 = 50% |50% |
|Average visit duration of A event |The sum of the duration of the event divided by the total number of sessions in which the event occurred. |The duration of the A event is the time between A and the next event, or 0 if A is the last event of the session. For example, the duration of the A event in session1 is 10 minutes between the occurrence times of A and B. With the addition of 1 minute difference between the occurrence times of A and C, the total is 11 minutes. There is no A event in session2 and session5, which is 0. Session3 and session4 are the last events in the session, with a duration of 0. Therefore, the duration of the A event for the numerator is 11 minutes, and the denominator is 3 sessions containing the occurrence of the A event. |11/3 |
|Mean depth of visits |The sum of the number of access events within the session (without duplication)/the total number of access sessions |The depth of session1 is 4, the depth of session2 is 2, the depth of session3 is 3, the depth of session4 is 1, the depth of session5 is 1, the mean numerator of depth of visit is: 4 + 2 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 11, and the denominator is: the total number of sessions 5. |2.2 |


<span id="_3-功能介绍"></span>
# 3. Function introduction

Growth Analytics provides you with the ability to customize sessions. After creating a custom session, you can choose to switch session analysis in the event analysis tool. The main operating process is as follows.


1. Create a custom session in the **custom session** interface of **data management** , and define the events to be analyzed in this custom session, the segmentation strategy of the session, etc.

2. Enter the **event analysis** page, switch to session analysis, configure parameters such as analysis indicators, and view the analysis query result data.


For detailed operation steps, please refer to: [Custom Session](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Custom_Session) .
